messages:
alex_nguyen: Heads-up — NVIDIA released driver 535.86.05 with a reported privilege escalation in the kgd module. CVE-2025-1234. Need triage for Dedicated/Docker GPU images and a compatibility validation plan. Any immediate blockers?

maria_schechter: CVE id? severity score? link?

alex_nguyen: CVE-2025-1234, link: https://nvidia.com/security/driver/535.86.05 (internal mirror copied). NVD CVSS 8.1. Privilege escalation in kernel graphics driver. Likely affects driver bundles we ship inside redwood/gpu-runtime images pinned to 535.*

kevin_chen: I ran image-scan last night, see results from infra-bot below. Affected images: redwood/gpu-runtime:ubuntu20.04-cu118 (driver 535.80), redwood/dedicated-gpu:cu118-rt (custom installer). We need to rebuild those with the patched driver and run matrix tests for CUDA/cuDNN/NCCL compatibility. Also check onprem installer bundles.

infra-bot: [scan-report] gpu-stack-scan found vulnerable kgd in 2 images: redwood/gpu-runtime:ubuntu20.04-cu118@sha256:... , redwood/dedicated-gpu:cu118-rt@sha256:... . Risk: HIGH. Recommended action: rebuild with driver 535.86.05, run gpu-compat-matrix CI. (automated)

oncall_sre: If we rebuild driver in the image, what about host kernels for Dedicated? Some customers run in Dedicated with host-driver mapping (NVIDIA driver on host). We should confirm which deployments rely on host drivers vs bundled drivers.

maria_schechter: Good point. For Dedicated we typically rely on host drivers. For Hosted API we run containers with NVIDIA driver shipped in image for legacy reasons — we need inventory. Kevin do we have a list mapping clusters->driver strategy?

kevin_chen: I'll pull from infra assets. Quick plan:
- Inventory: identify clusters/images using bundled driver vs host-driver (job: infra/gpu-driver-inventory)
- Rebuild images that bundle drivers with 535.86.05 (CI job: gpu-rebuild-driver)
- Run compatibility matrix: driver x CUDA x cuDNN x NCCL (job: gpu-compat-matrix)
- Canary rollout: deploy to staging canary pool (tag: canary-gpu-1), smoke tests (job: gpu-smoketest), perf benchmark (job: gpu-bench)
- Schedule Dedicated host-driver upgrades with customer ops for maintenance windows

alex_nguyen: Also propose we sign the rebuilt driver artifacts and store in artifact repo with KMS-backed key. This will let onprem installers verify integrity. We should also update audit logs for driver publish events.

maria_schechter: Agree. Action items and owners?

kevin_chen: Assigning:
- kevin_chen: run inventory + rebuild images
- alex_nguyen: driver signing + artifact publish with KMS (key: projects/redwood-kms/keys/driver-sign)
- maria_schechter: coordinate Dedicated host upgrades + customer comms
- oncall_sre: prepare rollback playbook and emergency patch channel

infra-bot: Created issues: RD-2384 (inventory), RD-2385 (image rebuild), RD-2386 (compat matrix), RD-2387 (canary rollout). Links: https://issues.redwood/RED-2384

oncall_sre: Rollback notes: cordon affected nodes, drain workloads, revert to previous image tag, re-enable scheduling. Commands for quick revert:
```
kubectl cordon gpu-canary-01
kubectl drain gpu-canary-01 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
kubectl set image deploy/gpu-runtime-deploy gpu-runtime=redwood/gpu-runtime:ubuntu20.04-cu118@sha256:<prev>
```
Also have kernel module unload script if host-driver change: `/usr/local/bin/uninstall-nvidia.sh`.

maria_schechter: Prioritization: Hosted API images that directly impact low-latency inference get P0 rebuild. Dedicated host-driver upgrades P1 until customer-scheduled windows confirmed. Onprem customers — reach out via account teams.

alex_nguyen: Timeline proposal: inventory + image rebuilds in 24h, compatibility CI 48h, canary rollout 72h. If CI fails, stop and triage. Approve?

kevin_chen: ack. Starting inventory now.

maria_schechter: I'll draft customer notices and update runbook.

oncall_sre: tagging incident channel #inc-kgd for visibility. :rotating_light:

alex_nguyen: Thanks team — post updates here. We'll close RD-2384/5/6 when done.
